title: Time-and-Materials Billing Rules for Professional Services Projects
content:
Professional Services Projects time-and-materials work is logged per person level, time band and day, with minutes rounded up to the class billing increment, and an onsite day is never billed below the class minimum onsite hours.

## Monthly invoice

On the first day of each month the previous month's work is invoiced. Each log line is priced as its worked minutes divided by 60, multiplied by the class hourly rate of the person level (technician, senior engineer or solutions architect), reduced by the engagement's rate discount, and multiplied by the class after-hours multiplier for scheduled after-hours work. Each log line is rounded half up to the cent, and the rounded lines are summed into the invoice.

| Time band of the log line | Multiplier |
|---|---|
| scheduled after-hours window | the class after-hours multiplier |
| business hours | none (the rate stands) |

## Not-to-exceed amount

Billing never takes the engagement's time-and-materials billings above its contract value, the not-to-exceed amount, because work beyond it may not be billed without a signed change order: work beyond it needs a signed change order raising the amount. The client is notified when billings reach the class alert percentage of that amount.

## Prepaid TimeBank hours

Where the class allows drawing on prepaid hours and the client holds a TimeBank block whose status is active and which is eligible for project work, logged time is settled from the block (billing route timebank) under the TimeBank conversion rules instead of being invoiced, and only time beyond the block balance is invoiced.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A log line records 90 minutes of after-hours work at a hypothetical rate of 200.00 per hour, on an engagement whose rate discount is 5.0 percent, with a multiplier of 1.5. The line is 90 divided by 60, that is 1.5 hours, multiplied by 200.00, giving 300.00; reduced by 5.0 percent, giving 285.00; multiplied by 1.5, giving 427.50. The line is rounded to the cent (427.50) before it is added to the month's other lines.
